bug_semantics: The schema-text fallback selected a sibling image, read its raw alt attribute, and concatenated that value into a double-quoted HTML attribute. A quote in attacker-controlled alt text could terminate the attribute and create an onload or other event-handler attribute when a consumer parsed or rendered the returned HTML. The pre-return sanitizer could not remove the newly formed handler because it ran on the source DOM before this string construction.
flaw_origin: Commit 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c added _findContentBySchemaText and, in the same atomic single-parent commit, first wrote html += `` using the raw sibling alt value. Its immediate parent 2875898370e1226c0aa1fd92ccb511465f025eb0 has neither the method nor imageSrc/imageAlt handling.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c shows author and committer Steph Ango <10565871+kepano@users.noreply.github.com>, one parent, subject 'Support for Substack app', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: git log -L 146,218:src/defuddle.ts 7cd4a27447b42e596b38a102428b20194c39c316^ traces the complete vulnerable _findContentBySchemaText method to 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c, where the 73-line method and the raw imageAlt interpolation first appear.

git show 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c^:src/defuddle.ts followed by searches for _findContentBySchemaText, imageSrc, and imageAlt returns no matches; git cat-file identifies the exact immediate parent as 2875898370e1226c0aa1fd92ccb511465f025eb0.

git show 7cd4a27447b42e596b38a102428b20194c39c316 -- src/defuddle.ts shows the direct fix: create an img DOM element, set src and alt with setAttribute, then append img.outerHTML, replacing the unsafe template interpolation.

git merge-base --is-ancestor proves the vulnerable sequence 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c -> f154cb740ee603431b69638273af737a27156df9 -> 7cd4a27447b42e596b38a102428b20194c39c316; f154cb740ee603431b69638273af737a27156df9 only hardened the source DOM and did not directly fix the later string-construction sink.

The npm registry metadata identifies defuddle 0.7.0 gitHead as 9a49b7a30d22ea7e3df754ae63898161693a65c6 and 0.8.0 gitHead as fef3f67381e5eb3d5a5cc574c7f15e14ea5a7d56; git grep at both exact trees finds _findContentBySchemaText absent, and neither release commit contains the BIC.

The npm registry identifies 0.9.0 gitHead as 440f9e8ca92a7be7871aeb07200190328340dbbf, published 2026-03-05T19:15:02.037Z; ancestry checks show it contains both BIC 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c and direct fix 7cd4a27447b42e596b38a102428b20194c39c316.

Git tag containment agrees with the registry boundary: neither 0.7.0 nor 0.8.0 contains the BIC, while 0.9.0 contains both BIC and fix; the vulnerable code existed only in unreleased history between 2026-03-04T10:23:58-08:00 and 2026-03-05T10:39:23-08:00.

GitHub's live advisory API reports GHSA-5mq8-78gm-pjmq as not withdrawn and claims npm defuddle <= 0.7.0 is vulnerable with 0.9.0 first patched, but the exact published 0.7.0 tree predates and lacks the vulnerable method; this makes the released-package claim a false positive.

The live CVE.org record at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-30830 is PUBLISHED and claims versions < 0.9.0 affected, but the repository and npm gitHead topology directly contradict that release range: 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 lack the mechanism and 0.9.0 contains its fix.
The BIC commit object has a human author and committer, no trailers, no bot identity, and no AI marker; AI attribution is therefore absent on the only commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism.
reasoning: The flaw itself was real in a short unreleased main-branch interval: 7b9c01b8dc979f2dff5e308ac55c0ffa350dd51c first added the schema fallback and unsafe raw-alt interpolation, its parent lacks the whole mechanism, f154cb740ee603431b69638273af737a27156df9 sanitized the pre-construction DOM without closing this sink, and 7cd4a27447b42e596b38a102428b20194c39c316 directly replaced interpolation with DOM serialization. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, so no squash decomposition is available or needed, and its commit object has no AI marker. Release topology changes the advisory verdict: published npm 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 both predate and lack the BIC, while the first later release, 0.9.0, contains the direct fix. Thus no published npm version in either the GHSA's <= 0.7.0 range or CVE.org's < 0.9.0 range contains this vulnerability. Although both records remain published, their released-package vulnerability assertion is a false positive rather than a real vulnerable release attributable to AI or a human.
